fact: The article says telecoms licensees' spectrum obligations align with the government's SA Connect target of universal broadband access with an average user experience of 100Mbps by 2030, a period not ended; the document gives no event date, so its published date 2026-08-03 is used.

ICASA says its IMT Roadmap supports national broadband objectives as outlined in the SA Connect Broadband Policy, which it treats as in force and cites for broadband access; the document gives no period for the policy and no event date, so its published date 2026-07-28 is used.

ICASA's media statement names the SA Connect Broadband Policy as an existing national policy that the IMT Roadmap 2026 supports, and gives no period or successor for it; no date is given for the policy, so the document's published date is used.
The page on the IMT Roadmap 2026 gazette names "broadband for all" as set in the SA Connect policy of 2013, and states no period or successor for that policy.
Deputy Minister Gungubele cites the department's South African National Broadband Policy, with the Digital Economy Master Plan, as aiming to provide infrastructure for digital education and skills.

The Minister of Communications published the Broadband Policy for South Africa as Government Notice 617 under the Electronic Communications Act on 13 July 2010, with targets of universal access to broadband, 15 percent household penetration and connectivity to all municipal areas, each by 2019; the document gives no end or successor.

The Department of Communications and Digital Technologies' draft data and cloud policy of 1 April 2021 refers to South Africa Connect and the National Broadband Policy as existing inclusion strategies with broadband access targets for 2030; it gives no adoption date, so its published date is used.
